title: Sharon Osbourne Urges Fans to 'Play Music Loud' as World Marks One Year Since Ozzy's Death
excerpt: The Osbourne family shares emotional tributes on the first anniversary of the Black Sabbath frontman's death, while his hometown of Birmingham celebrates its inaugural 'Ozzy Day.'
body:
• Sharon Osbourne has asked fans to honour Ozzy's memory by playing his music loud on the first anniversary of his death on July 22.
  • Daughter Kelly Osbourne posted an emotional Instagram tribute describing grief as an "endless ache" and mourning "the soul I was before death taught my heart its own name."
  • Birmingham, Ozzy's hometown, is celebrating its inaugural "Ozzy Day" with live music, public art and performances at landmarks tied to the rocker's legacy.
  • The Osbourne family is also developing a "Digital Ozzy" AI avatar to preserve his legacy for future generations of fans.

Sharon Osbourne has called on fans worldwide to turn up the volume on the first anniversary of her husband Ozzy Osbourne's death, urging them to play his music loud in tribute to the man who helped invent heavy metal.

The Black Sabbath co-founder and solo rock icon died on July 22, 2025, at age 76. His death certificate listed his cause of death as a heart attack, citing coronary heart disease and Parkinson's disease, and recorded his occupation as "Songwriter, Performer and Rock Legend."

A Family's Year of Grief

The anniversary has drawn raw, deeply personal tributes from across the Osbourne family. Daughter Kelly Osbourne, 41, published a lengthy letter on Instagram titled "What I've come to know about grief in the last year," confronting the toll of losing her father in unflinching terms.

"There is a grief that steals more than the person you love. It quietly takes the light from your laughter, the innocence from your hope, and the stranger you become is someone you'll spend a lifetime trying to recognise," Kelly wrote. She described the loss as an "endless ache," adding: "Some losses don't simply break you. They divide your life into two people. The one you were before, and the one left behind."

Earlier this month, Sharon marked what would have been the couple's 46th wedding anniversary on July 4 with her own Instagram tribute. "Today would have been our 46th wedding anniversary. Instead, it is a celebration of a love that even death could not diminish," she wrote alongside a photograph of their hands clasped together. "I miss your hand in mine, but I carry your love with me every step of the way. Forever my husband. Forever my heart."

"I don't just mourn the father I lost. I mourn the soul I was before death taught my heart its own name."

— Kelly Osbourne, in an Instagram tribute on the first anniversary of Ozzy's death

Birmingham's Inaugural 'Ozzy Day'

In Ozzy's hometown of Birmingham, England, the anniversary is being marked with the city's first-ever "Ozzy Day" — a free, citywide celebration of his life and legacy. The event features live music, public art, special performances and fan tributes at landmarks closely tied to Osbourne's story, including the Black Sabbath Bench and Bridge, the Birmingham Museum & Art Gallery, and the Bullring shopping centre.

The City of Birmingham Symphony Orchestra and Bostin Brass are among the performers. Ozzy the Bull — the giant mechanical sculpture created for the 2022 Commonwealth Games and later named after the rocker — is receiving a special Ozzy-inspired makeover for the occasion.

"Ozzy Day is a fantastic example of Birmingham working together to celebrate the legendary Ozzy Osbourne," said Sam Watson, chair of Central BID Birmingham. "By bringing together businesses, cultural organisations and public spaces, we're creating a city centre wide experience that encourages people to celebrate the legacy of a truly global, Birmingham-born icon."

A separate campaign to rename Birmingham Airport to "Ozzy Osbourne International" has attracted over 70,000 signatures, with Sharon giving it her backing: "The world loved Ozzy. It's just a dream right now but sometimes dreams come true."

Legacy Beyond the Grave

Ozzy died just 17 days after his triumphant "Back to the Beginning" farewell concert at Villa Park, which reunited Black Sabbath's original lineup — Tony Iommi, Geezer Butler and Bill Ward — for one final performance. The event raised funds for Cure Parkinson's, Birmingham Children's Hospital and Acorns Children's Hospice.

"The one you were before, and the one left behind."</p> <p>Earlier this month, Sharon marked what would have been the couple's 46th wedding anniversary on July 4 with her own Instagram tribute."

Son Jack Osbourne, 40, has spoken in recent months about how the family is processing the loss. "Ozzy Osbourne does not end because he passed away on July 22. He's just exploding through the universe and we're all seeing it," he said in a video tribute shortly after his father's death.

The family has also been developing "Digital Ozzy," an AI-powered avatar built from a closed database of Ozzy's own words and verified biographical material. Jack has defended the project against accusations that it amounts to a cash grab, saying his father discussed the idea before his death and would have supported it. "It's not about pretending he's still alive. For me it's about making sure he's never forgotten," Jack said on The Osbournes Podcast.

For fans across the globe — from Birmingham to Bangalore — the message from the Osbourne family is simple: honour the Prince of Darkness the way he would have wanted. Play the music loud.
